tours.intro: Three days through the northern mountains, from the valleys of Du Gia to the limestone scenery around Dong Van. Discover waterfalls, river views and mountain passes, then return to Ha Giang through Yen Minh. Choose this route when your time is limited and you are comfortable with a fuller second day.

itinerary.title: Ha Giang to Du Gia
itinerary.path: Ha Giang → Bac Sum Pass → Quan Ba Twin Mountains → pine-hill stop → Du Gia
itinerary.text: Leave Ha Giang and follow the mountain roads towards Quan Ba. Pause at Bac Sum and the Twin Mountains viewpoints, then take a pine-hill break before continuing to Du Gia. The local team confirms the pine viewpoint and connecting road to suit the day's conditions and timing.

itinerary.title: Waterfall, river & high mountain views
itinerary.path: Du Gia Waterfall → Nho Que River / Ma Pi Leng → Skywalk → Dong Van
itinerary.text: Start with Du Gia Waterfall, then continue towards the Nho Que River and Ma Pi Leng area. River access and pass viewpoints are sequenced locally to allow time for the descent and return. A boat trip is an option to confirm in the quote, not an automatic inclusion. Add a Skywalk viewpoint walk only when local access, weather and the group's ability allow; finish in Dong Van.
itinerary.stay: Proposed overnight: Dong Van. This is the most activity-heavy day.

itinerary.title: Village craft & the road back
itinerary.path: Dong Van → Tham Ma Pass → Yen Minh → weaving village → waterfall stop → Ha Giang
itinerary.text: Return via Tham Ma Pass and Yen Minh. Lung Tam is the proposed weaving-village visit in the Quan Ba area, offering a chance to learn about Hmong hemp textiles and handweaving when the workshop is open. A final waterfall stop is subject to a suitable location and time on the return route, agreed before booking. Finish in Ha Giang and arrange onward-transfer timing separately.
itinerary.stay: Finish: Ha Giang. No overnight stay included in this itinerary after the return.

itinerary.title: Ha Giang, Quan Ba & Duong Thuong
itinerary.path: Ha Giang → Bac Sum Pass → Quan Ba Twin Mountains → pine-hill stop / Duong Thuong → Du Gia
itinerary.text: Begin in Ha Giang and climb towards Bac Sum Pass and the Quan Ba Twin Mountains. A pine-hill stop offers a change of pace before the valley roads through Duong Thuong and the onward journey to Du Gia. itinerary.title: Du Gia to the Nho Que & Ma Pi Leng area
itinerary.path: Du Gia Waterfall → Nho Que River / Ma Pi Leng → Skywalk → Dong Van
itinerary.text: Visit Du Gia Waterfall, then travel towards the dramatic river-and-pass scenery around Ma Pi Leng. The Nho Que visit, optional boat arrangements and viewpoint stops are timed together to avoid a rushed river descent. A Skywalk visit is conditional on access, conditions and suitable ability. Continue to Dong Van for the proposed second night.
itinerary.stay: Proposed overnight: Dong Van. Allow flexibility on this activity-heavy day.

itinerary.title: Lung Cu & the northern frontier

itinerary.text: Head north towards Lung Cu Flag Tower for the frontier chapter of the journey. A locally permitted border viewpoint on the Vietnam side can be considered with the guide; this is not a crossing into China. Return towards Tham Ma Pass and Yen Minh, with the exact frontier stop agreed locally before booking.

itinerary.path: Yen Minh → weaving village → waterfall stop → Ha Giang
itinerary.text: Continue towards Quan Ba for the proposed Lung Tam weaving-village visit. Learn about Hmong hemp cloth and the patient work behind local textiles; workshop access is confirmed in advance. Include the requested final waterfall only once the team has confirmed a suitable location and time on the return route. Finish in Ha Giang, with any onward transfer arranged separately.

faqs.q: Should I choose the 3-day or 4-day Ha Giang Loop?
faqs.a: Both routes feature Du Gia, Nho Que River and Ma Pi Leng. The 3-day version returns on day three; the 4-day version adds a Lung Cu and northern-frontier day, plus a proposed third night in Yen Minh.

faqs.q: Is the Nho Que boat trip included?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Boat tickets, local transfers and any other optional experience are charged separately unless they are listed in your written quote. Your guide will explain the practical options and help shape the day around your time, weather and comfort.

faqs.q: Does the route cross the Chinese border?
faqs.a: No. The 4-day itinerary may include a locally permitted viewpoint on the Vietnam side. The exact stop is confirmed with the local team.

faqs.q: Which weaving village and return-day waterfall will we visit?
faqs.a: Lung Tam is the proposed weaving-village stop, subject to workshop access and route timing. The return-day waterfall is chosen with your guide according to the road, weather and available time. Any added entrance, transfer or activity fee is explained before it is added.

faqs.q: What are the prices and how do I get from Hanoi to Ha Giang?
faqs.a: The prices are USD 200–226 per person for 3 days / 2 nights and USD 250–270 per person for 4 days / 3 nights, including Hanoi pickup and coach travel to Ha Giang City. Your exact price, coach type and timing are confirmed before travel. Other services and return or onward transport are itemised in writing. Private tours receive a tailored quote.

First share your dates, group size and route. We then confirm the price, included services and any separately charged options in writing. Your guide can suggest a practical plan before you decide. Pay only the agreed deposit to a verified official recipient; the deposit amount, payment method and booking conditions are confirmed directly before payment.

Yes. Road conditions, river access, waterfall conditions and viewpoint access can change the plan. Your local guide will recommend safer alternatives and help adjust the order of stops. Skywalk visits are conditional; do not enter closed trails or stop for photos on an active roadway.

faqs.q: What services or activities may cost extra?
faqs.a: Optional boat rides, extra entrance tickets, special room requests, private transfers, additional meals or activities outside the agreed route may be charged separately. We explain each item before adding it, and your guide can suggest the best-value choice for your group.

faqs.q: Can someone help us plan the right route?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us your dates, group size, pace and priorities. A local guide can suggest stops, timing and practical alternatives so the route fits your group instead of becoming a rushed checklist. For detailed advice, contact us by Gmail or WhatsApp.

faqs.q: How can I ask for more information?
faqs.a: For a detailed quote or questions about pickup, optional services and the route, contact us by Gmail or WhatsApp. We will clarify what is included, what is optional and what should be confirmed before you book.
